gloss: don't be absurd; that's out of the question

definitions.gloss: don't be absurd; that's out of the question; not at all
definitions.explanation: An emphatic denial or humble refusal used when someone suggests something the speaker considers unthinkable, excessive, or undeserved. Often used to modestly deflect praise or decline an offer.

examples.japanese: 「お⟦{上手|じょうず}→上手：00707_jouzu⟧です⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。」「{滅相|めっそう}もない。」
{滅相|めっそう}もない、⟦そんな→そんな：01645_sonna⟧{大|おお}それたこと⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦できません→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: That's out of the question—I couldn't do something so presumptuous.

examples.japanese: 「⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}って→座る：00757_suwaru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。」「{滅相|めっそう}もない、お⟦やめ→やめる：00909_yameru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。」
examples.english: "May I sit in the president's chair?" "Absolutely not—please don't."

notes:
USAGE:
A strongly humble or emphatic expression used to deny or refuse something. Two main uses:
1. Humble deflection of praise or flattery (like "Oh no, not at all!")
2. Emphatic rejection of a suggestion as absurd or inappropriate

REGISTER:
Somewhat formal and old-fashioned. More commonly heard from older speakers or in formal situations. Younger speakers tend to use ⟦とんでもない→とんでもない：03470_tondemonai⟧ instead.

FORMS:
- {滅相|めっそう}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ございませ→ございます：01300_gozaimasu⟧ん: very polite form
- {滅相|めっそう}もないこと⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧: "what an absurd thing to say"

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦とんでもない→とんでもない：03470_tondemonai⟧: no way, not at all — modern equivalent, widely used
- ⟦{恐|おそ}れ{入|い}ります→恐れ入る：05914_osoreiru⟧: I'm much obliged — humble, used when receiving praise
